facet_contributions.possible_uses: 用于回答“肠道微生物群如何调节ICIs疗效”中的相关性证据部分。可用于构建“菌群特征-治疗响应”的映射关系，或作为讨论个体差异来源的依据。

facet_contributions.possible_uses: 用于回答“哪些机制介导了这种效应”。提供具体的信号通路、细胞互作和代谢途径，支持对因果关系的理论解释。

review_planning_B.planning_summary: 该综述为“肠道微生物群如何调节实体瘤免疫检查点抑制剂疗效及机制”这一主题提供了详尽的背景、机制解释和临床证据汇总。它特别适合作为解释GM-免疫轴生物学基础的核心素材，以及用于对比不同干预策略（如FMT vs 益生菌 vs 饮食）有效性与局限性的参考。文中提供的具体菌株、代谢物和临床试验信息可直接用于构建证据图谱。
scope_interpretation_cautions: 该综述涵盖多种癌症类型（黑色素瘤、肺癌、肾癌、肝癌等），在应用其发现时需注意癌症类型的特异性，不能将所有实体瘤的结果一概而论。
文中提到的机制很多基于前临床模型（小鼠），在推断人体机制时需保持谨慎，区分动物实验结果与临床验证结果。
临床证据主要来自回顾性队列或小规模前瞻性研究，存在选择偏倚和混杂因素（如合并用药、饮食记录缺失），关联不等于因果。
干预措施（如益生菌、FMT）的效果高度依赖于供体/菌株特异性、给药时机和患者基线菌群状态，综述中的成功案例不代表普遍适用性。

study_summary_A.approach: 作为一篇综述，本研究采用文献综合方法。通过检索PubMed、Web of Science等多个数据库（截至2026年5月），筛选关于肠道微生物群、系统性免疫、免疫检查点抑制剂及癌症治疗的文献。内容组织逻辑为：1. GM基础与抗肿瘤功能概述；2. GM调节系统性免疫的机制（包括代谢物作用、免疫细胞分化）；3. GM对ICIs疗效及毒性的具体影响（分前临床和临床研究）；4. 基于GM的干预策略（饮食、益生菌、益生元、抗生素、FMT）；5. 未来展望与挑战。文中引用了大量具体的菌株、代谢物、受体通路及临床试验ID作为支撑材料。

contribution_and_limits.contribution: 提供了肠道微生物群调节ICIs疗效的系统性机制框架，涵盖了从菌群组成、代谢物信号到免疫细胞互作的多层次联系；汇总了针对多种实体瘤（黑色素瘤、NSCLC、肾癌等）的临床队列数据，识别了潜在的预测性生物标志物；全面评估了五种主要GM调控策略（饮食、益生菌、益生元、抗生素、FMT）的证据等级及临床应用现状。
contribution_and_limits.limits: 作为综述，其结论依赖于已发表研究的异质性结果，不同研究间菌群特征与疗效关联存在不一致性（如某些菌在不同癌症类型中作用相反）；许多机制仍基于动物模型，人体内的因果链条尚未完全确立；缺乏标准化的微生物组分析协议和临床干预方案，限制了结果的直接外推和临床转化；未提供新的原始实验数据。

key_findings.finding: 有益菌群（如Bifidobacterium, Akkermansia muciniphila, Collinsella aerofaciens）的富集与更好的客观缓解率和生存期相关；其机制涉及激活树突状细胞、促进CD8+ T细胞浸润及产生IL-12。相反，某些菌群（如部分Bacteroides）或与耐药相关。
厚壁菌门（Firmicutes），特别是Faecalibacterium属，与较好的治疗响应相关；而拟杆菌门（Bacteroidetes）的某些物种可能与较差预后或结肠炎毒性相关。
短链脂肪酸（SCFAs，如丁酸盐、丙酸盐）可通过抑制组蛋白去乙酰化酶（HDAC）或激活GPCR来调节Treg/Th17平衡及T细胞功能，但其作用具有情境依赖性（如在抗PD-1中可能有益，而在抗CTLA-4中高血清水平可能预示不良预后）。肌苷（Inosine）可激活T细胞腺苷A2A受体增强ICI疗效。
FMT从ICI响应者转移至非响应者小鼠或患者，可恢复对PD-1阻断的敏感性；特定益生菌（如Bifidobacterium pseudolongum）或益生元（如菊粉）可增强抗肿瘤免疫；广谱抗生素通常损害ICI疗效，但特定抗生素（如万古霉素）在某些模型中可能有益。

study_summary_A.problem_or_question: 肠道微生物群如何通过其组成和代谢产物调节宿主系统性免疫，进而决定癌症免疫检查点抑制剂（ICIs）的治疗响应率、耐药性及毒性？有哪些基于GM的干预策略可以优化免疫治疗效果？
study_summary_A.research_scope: 人类肠道微生物群（GM）与系统性免疫反应及癌症免疫治疗（特别是免疫检查点抑制剂，ICIs）之间的相互作用。涵盖从基础机制到临床转化及干预策略的综合讨论。
study_summary_A.work_summary: 本文是一篇综述，旨在系统梳理肠道微生物群如何调节全身免疫系统并影响癌症免疫治疗的疗效与毒性。文章首先概述了GM的组成及其在维持免疫稳态中的作用，随后深入探讨了GM通过特定菌群（如双歧杆菌、阿克曼氏菌等）及其代谢产物（如短链脂肪酸、肌苷、胆汁酸）调节T细胞、树突状细胞等免疫细胞功能，进而影响肿瘤微环境的机制。接着，文章总结了前临床（小鼠模型）和临床研究证据，展示了GM组成与ICI（抗PD-1/PD-L1、抗CTLA-4）疗效及免疫相关不良反应（irAEs）的相关性。最后，文章评估了通过饮食干预、益生菌、益生元、抗生素及粪便微生物移植（FMT）等GM调控手段优化免疫治疗效果的潜力与挑战。

supplement_gap_material.remaining_gap: This study does not report the absolute physiological concentrations (e.g., μmol/g or μM) of inosine or SCFAs required by the success criteria. It references external primary studies for metabolite associations but does not reproduce the specific quantitative data. Furthermore, while it mentions metabolites propagating to tumor sites, it does not confirm measured concentrations within human tumor tissue itself; the inosine finding is explicitly linked to mouse models in the preclinical section. The text does not specify whether the cited human metabolite studies (Botticelli, Coutzac) were prospective or if they utilized paired tumor tissue and serum/stool sampling.
supplement_gap_material.useful_material: This study identifies inosine and short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) as key microbiota-derived metabolites influencing immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) response. It reports that Bifidobacterium pseudolongum-derived inosine improves antitumor actions via activation of adenosine A2A receptors on T cells, citing preclinical evidence (Mager et al. 2020). For SCFAs, it notes that increased fecal propionic acid in anti-PD-1 patients correlates with increased antitumor responses and prolonged survival (Botticelli et al. 2020), while increased serum butyrate in anti-CTLA-4 patients links to poor outcomes (Coutzac et al. 2020a, b). Mechanisms described include SCFA-mediated histone deacetylase (HDAC) suppression and G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) activation. The text distinguishes between metabolite effects in different treatment contexts (anti-PD-1 vs. anti-CTLA-4) and compartments (fecal vs. serum).

candidate_materials.title: Gut microbiota modulation of systemic immunity and cancer immunotherapy: mechanisms, evidence, and therapeutic implications

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 用于说明当前领域的局限性、未来研究方向（标准化、大样本RCT、多中心合作）以及为何需要更严谨的综合分析。
broader_review_uses.material: 综述指出当前证据多为中等或低确定性，方法学异质性大（采样、测序、终点定义不一），缺乏标准化和高确定性RCT证据。黑色素瘤研究占主导，其他肿瘤类型（如血液瘤、胃肠道癌）研究不足。

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 可作为评估不同微生物干预策略相对价值的定性比较框架，帮助读者理解不同干预手段在现有证据下的整体趋势。
broader_review_uses.material: 提出了“跨干预措施元效应评分”这一概念，将FMT、高纤维饮食、Vidutolimod评为正向（+1.0），抗生素、益生菌评为负向（-1.0）。

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: 用于讨论微生物疗法临床转化的实际障碍、监管环境和临床实践建议，超越单纯的科学发现，涵盖实施科学层面。
broader_review_uses.material: 讨论了FMT的伦理和监管挑战（病原体传播、长期效应、供体选择），以及EMA/FDA指南的不完善。建议优化抗生素使用，避免非靶向益生菌。

facet_contributions.boundaries: 多数为观察性关联，因果方向需谨慎解读；黑色素瘤数据最多，其他肿瘤类型证据较弱；干预性研究（如FMT）样本量小，存在偏倚风险。
facet_contributions.contribution: 提供了肠道微生物群特征（多样性、特定菌属丰度）与ICI疗效（ORR, PFS, OS）之间关联的大量临床观察证据。明确了高多样性和有益菌富集与良好预后的正相关，以及抗生素/益生菌使用的负相关。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 用于回答“肠道微生物群如何调节ICI疗效”中的描述性问题：哪些微生物特征与疗效相关？可用于支持“微生物群是疗效关键决定因素”的观点，并提供具体菌属和多样性指标作为证据。

facet_contributions.boundaries: 许多机制细节主要来自基础或转化研究，文中指出这些机制在临床人群中的验证仍不充分；不同代谢物的浓度依赖性效应复杂（如butyrate的双刃剑效应）；机制链条在人体内的完整性和特异性尚未完全确立。
facet_contributions.contribution: 综述了已知的微生物-免疫机制通路，包括：inosine轴（Bifidobacterium pseudolongum -> A2A受体 -> CD8+ T细胞）、SCFAs（acetate/propionate -> DCs; butyrate -> Treg/memory T cells）、次级胆汁酸（Clostridium scindens -> TGR5 -> Th1 bias）和色氨酸代谢物（Fusobacterium nucleatum -> AhR -> 抑制T细胞趋化）。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 直接用于回答“介导效应的机制是什么”。提供具体的分子和细胞机制示例，解释微生物如何通过代谢物影响抗原呈递、T细胞浸润和功能。

facet_contributions.boundaries: 干预性研究多为早期阶段、单中心、小样本，证据等级中等；FMT的供体依赖性是一个重大挑战；饮食干预的自我报告偏差；Vidutolimod研究未根据微生物组成进行前瞻性分层，因果关系不明。
facet_contributions.contribution: 评估了多种微生物靶向干预策略的临床效果，包括FMT（ORR 20-40%）、高纤维饮食（改善PFS/OS）、Vidutolimod+Nivolumab（MPR ~55%），并对比了抗生素和益生菌的负面影响。引入了跨干预措施的元效应评分概念。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 用于回答“哪些微生物干预策略有效”的问题。提供不同干预手段的效果大小、适用人群（如难治性黑色素瘤）和潜在风险（如抗生素损害疗效）。可用于指导未来干预策略的选择和优先级排序。

facet_contributions.boundaries: 模型多在特定癌种（如直肠癌）中开发和小规模验证；需要大规模前瞻性验证才能临床常规应用；不同研究间的测序方法和算法差异限制了通用性。
facet_contributions.contribution: 介绍了基于微生物组的预测模型（如SPEED模型，AUC>0.75；ML分类器AUC 0.83-0.92）及其在患者分层和疗效预测中的潜力。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 用于讨论“如何利用微生物信息进行精准医疗”。提供预测模型的具体性能指标和应用场景（如直肠癌pCR预测），展示微生物组从生物标志物向临床决策工具的转变。

review_planning_B.planning_summary: 该综述为理解肠道微生物群如何作为ICI疗效的关键决定因素提供了全面的临床视角。它不仅汇总了微生物特征（多样性、特定菌属）与预后的关联，还详细评估了多种干预手段（FMT、饮食、抗生素、益生菌、药物组合）的临床效果，并引入了跨干预措施的定性比较框架。对于综述而言，它是梳理“微生物-免疫-疗效”关系、识别关键干预靶点（如避免抗生素、利用FMT/饮食）以及理解当前方法学局限性的核心素材。
scope_interpretation_cautions: 该综述主要为叙事性综合，非系统性荟萃分析，结果不应被解读为经过严格统计合并的效应量估计。
大部分证据来自观察性研究或小规模早期临床试验，因果推断需谨慎，特别是关于抗生素和益生菌的负面效应，可能存在混杂因素。
黑色素瘤数据最为丰富，对其他实体瘤的结论外推时需考虑肿瘤特异性和微环境差异。
机制部分引用的分子通路多基于基础或转化研究，其在广泛临床人群中的普遍性和重要性仍需更多临床验证。
预测模型的AUC值来自不同研究，直接比较其性能需谨慎，因训练集、验证集和特征工程可能存在差异。

study_summary_A.approach: 采用叙事性综述方法。检索PubMed/MEDLINE、Embase和Cochrane Library数据库（2015-2025年），筛选出评估肠道微生物群与癌症免疫治疗关系的95项人类临床研究。由两名审稿人独立提取数据并进行偏倚风险评估（使用Cochrane RoB 2、ROBINS-I等工具）。由于研究设计和结局的高度异质性，未进行正式荟萃分析，而是采用结构化叙述综合，强调机制合理性、转化相关性和跨癌症类型/干预模式的一致性。此外，还进行了跨干预措施的元效应评分分析以定性比较不同干预措施的临床价值。

contribution_and_limits.contribution: 提供了截至2025年关于肠道微生物群影响ICI疗效的全面临床证据综述，特别强调了抗生素和益生菌的负面作用以及FMT和高纤维饮食的潜在益处。
contribution_and_limits.limits: 所给摘要未交代具体的文献检索式细节（除关键词外）；由于研究异质性大，无法进行定量荟萃分析；证据等级多为中等或低等，缺乏高确定性证据；黑色素瘤研究占主导，其他肿瘤类型的泛化性受限；观察性研究多，因果推断能力有限。

key_findings.conditions: 接受ICI治疗的实体瘤患者（特别是黑色素瘤和NSCLC）
key_findings.finding: 较高的基线肠道微生物多样性（尤其是Faith's系统发育多样性）与更好的无进展生存期（PFS）和总生存期（OS）相关；富集共生菌（如Akkermansia muciniphila, Ruminococcaceae, Faecalibacterium）及短链脂肪酸（SCFA）产生菌有助于改善疗效。

key_findings.conditions: ICI治疗期间或启动前30天内使用广谱抗生素
key_findings.finding: consistently与较差的临床结局相关，包括PFS和OS显著降低（死亡风险比HR 1.4-2.0），且这种负面影响跨越多种肿瘤类型，提示为类效应。

key_findings.conditions: 使用非靶向的商业混合益生菌
key_findings.finding: consistently与较差的ICI疗效相关（ORR降低，PFS缩短），可能原因是降低了微生物多样性并导致特定菌属过度代表。

key_findings.conditions: 来自ICI响应者的粪便微生物移植（FMT）
key_findings.finding: 在难治性黑色素瘤的早期I/II期临床试验中，客观缓解率（ORR）达到20-40%，部分患者出现持久反应；机制涉及供体微生物群的定植和抗肿瘤免疫激活（CD8+ T细胞浸润增加）。

key_findings.conditions: 高纤维饮食或植物导向型饮食干预
key_findings.finding: 与改善的PFS和OS相关，机制上促进SCFA产生菌（如Ruminococcaceae）的富集，增加粪便丁酸和乙酸水平，并与更高的肿瘤内T细胞浸润相关。

key_findings.conditions: 基于微生物组的预测模型（如SPEED模型）
key_findings.finding: 在直肠癌新辅助治疗中，SPEED模型预测病理完全缓解（pCR）的AUC超过0.75；整合16S或宏基因组特征的机器学习分类器预测ICI反应的AUC为0.83-0.92。

study_summary_A.problem_or_question: 尽管免疫检查点抑制剂（ICIs）改变了肿瘤学治疗格局，但其疗效在不同患者间差异巨大（仅20-40%获得持久获益）。除了PD-L1表达、TMB和MSI等传统生物标志物外，寻找能更准确预测疗效的新生物标志物并探索通过调节肠道微生物群来增强疗效的临床策略是当前的主要问题。
study_summary_A.research_scope: 人类临床研究中肠道微生物群与癌症免疫治疗（特别是免疫检查点抑制剂，ICI）疗效之间的关系。涵盖实体瘤（黑色素瘤、非小细胞肺癌、肾细胞癌等），时间跨度为2015年至2025年3月。
study_summary_A.work_summary: 这是一篇叙事性综述，旨在综合过去十年中关于肠道微生物群在调节癌症免疫治疗反应中的作用的临床证据。研究评估了微生物群作为预测生物标志物和靶向治疗靶点的功能，重点介绍了机制见解、临床干预措施和转化意义。通过对95项临床研究（包括随机试验、前瞻性队列、回顾性分析和早期阶段干预研究）的叙述性综合，论文总结了微生物多样性、特定菌属、饮食、抗生素使用、益生菌、粪便微生物移植（FMT）以及机器学习模型对ICI疗效的影响。

auxiliary_material: The review synthesized 95 clinical studies (2015–2025) but precluded formal meta-analysis due to methodological heterogeneity in sampling (stool versus mucosal biopsy) and sequencing.
A cross-intervention meta-effect score analysis rated FMT and dietary fiber as positive (+1.0) and antibiotics/probiotics as negative (−1.0), providing a qualitative framework for intervention value.
The authors explicitly state that variability in sample collection and lack of standardization hinder the comparison of metabolite data across studies.

Predictive models like SPEED (AUC > 0.75) and machine-learning classifiers (AUC 0.83–0.92) are mentioned as tools integrating microbiome profiles, though these focus on taxonomy or composite scores rather than absolute metabolite concentrations.

useful_material: This study identifies specific microbial metabolites mechanistically linked to ICI response, including inosine (via Bifidobacterium pseudolongum and A2A receptor on CD8+ T cells) and short-chain fatty acids (acetate, propionate, butyrate affecting dendritic cells and T-cell memory).

The authors report that metabolomic profiling in dietary fiber studies demonstrated higher fecal butyrate and acetate levels correlating with greater intratumoral T-cell infiltration, though absolute tumor tissue concentrations were not specified in this text.

This review notes that three metabolomic studies integrated microbiome and metabolite data to predict treatment outcomes (specifically adverse events with AUC 0.963 using fecal and plasma profiles), indicating the existence of quantitative metabolite datasets in the field.

The discussion highlights the complexity of metabolite stoichiometry and immune contexture, noting that high concentrations of butyrate can suppress IL-2-dependent memory formation while acetate/propionate enhance dendritic cell fitness.

candidate_materials.title: Clinical Evidence for Microbiome-Based Strategies in Cancer Immunotherapy: A State-of-the-Art Review

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: Helps establish the scientific basis for investigating GM-ICI interactions in solid tumors.
broader_review_uses.material: Introduction sections discussing the role of GMs in health and disease, and the rationale for combining GM modulation with ICIs and antiangiogenic therapy.
broader_review_uses.purpose: Contextual background on the importance of GMs in cancer therapy

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: Provides concrete examples of how GM modulation has been tested in clinical settings, including dosing, patient populations, and observed effects.
broader_review_uses.material: Tables 1, 2, and 3 listing various clinical trials involving ICIs, antiangiogenic agents, and GM-modulating interventions.
broader_review_uses.purpose: Examples of clinical trial designs and outcomes

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: Offers critical perspectives on the feasibility and risks of GM-based therapies, which can be contrasted with other reviews focusing solely on efficacy.
broader_review_uses.material: Sections on safety concerns (e.g., FMT-related infections), lack of specificity in probiotics, and individual variability.

facet_contributions.boundaries: Most evidence is correlative or from small-scale trials. Causality is often inferred from animal models. The paper notes variability in results across different cancer types.
facet_contributions.contribution: Provides a summary of clinical trials and observational studies showing associations between specific GM compositions (e.g., high abundance of Bifidobacterium, Akkermansia) and improved response to ICIs in solid tumors. Lists specific bacterial taxa and metabolites linked to better outcomes.
facet_contributions.possible_uses: Can be used to support arguments about the predictive value of baseline gut microbiome composition for ICI efficacy. Provides examples of successful combinations (e.g., FMT + Pembrolizumab).

facet_contributions.boundaries: Many mechanisms are derived from mouse models and may not fully translate to human physiology. The paper acknowledges that exact mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Some claims are based on limited human data.
facet_contributions.contribution: Details several proposed mechanisms by which GMs modulate ICI efficacy, including DC maturation, T-cell activation, and regulation of immunosuppressive cells (Tregs, MDSCs). Also describes mechanisms related to angiogenesis, such as metabolite-induced VEGF regulation.
facet_contributions.possible_uses: Useful for explaining potential biological pathways linking GMs to immune response. Can illustrate how different interventions (probiotics, FMT, diet) might exert effects via distinct mechanisms.

review_planning_B.planning_summary: This paper serves as a broad contextual resource for understanding the intersection of gut microbiome modulation, angiogenesis, and immune checkpoint inhibition. It provides a structured framework for discussing how GMs influence the tumor microenvironment and host immunity. While it does not offer deep mechanistic details for every pathway, it lists numerous specific bacterial species, metabolites, and clinical trial examples that can be used to illustrate the diversity of GM-therapy interactions. It is particularly useful for establishing the rationale for combining GM modulation with standard cancer therapies and for highlighting the current limitations in clinical translation.
scope_interpretation_cautions: This is a perspective/review article; findings are synthesized from other studies and should not be treated as primary empirical evidence.
Many mechanisms described are based on preclinical models; direct applicability to human patients is not confirmed.
The paper highlights heterogeneity in GM composition and response across individuals and cancer types, cautioning against over-generalization.
Claims about specific bacterial strains or metabolites are often based on limited or preliminary data.
topic_handles: Metabolites: Inosine, Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), LPS

study_summary_A.approach: As a perspective/review article, this work does not present new primary experimental data. Instead, it synthesizes existing literature from preclinical studies (mouse models) and clinical trials. The authors organize the content by first describing the composition and function of the gut microbiome, then detailing its impact on tumor angiogenesis and immune responses. They subsequently review various modulation strategies (probiotics, FMT, diet, engineering) and summarize relevant clinical trial data presented in tables. Finally, they discuss the translational challenges and future directions.

contribution_and_limits.contribution: Provides a comprehensive overview of the dual role of GMs in regulating both angiogenesis and immune checkpoint inhibition in cancer.
contribution_and_limits.limits: As a perspective piece, it relies on summarizing existing literature rather than generating new causal evidence. Many mechanisms described are based on preclinical models, and direct translation to humans remains uncertain.

contribution_and_limits.contribution: Summarizes a wide range of clinical trials and preclinical studies linking GM composition to ICI and antiangiogenic therapy outcomes.
contribution_and_limits.limits: The review does not provide a systematic meta-analysis or quantitative synthesis of the clinical data. Specificity of beneficial bacterial strains varies across studies, making generalization difficult.

contribution_and_limits.contribution: Identifies key challenges such as safety risks of FMT and lack of specificity in probiotic interventions.
contribution_and_limits.limits: Does not offer definitive solutions to these challenges but highlights them as areas for future research.

key_findings.conditions: Preclinical models and observational clinical data
key_findings.finding: Specific GMs (e.g., Bifidobacterium, Akkermansia muciniphila) and their metabolites (e.g., inosine, short-chain fatty acids) are associated with enhanced efficacy of ICIs by promoting dendritic cell maturation, T-cell activation, and reducing immunosuppressive cells.

key_findings.conditions: Mechanistic studies in vitro and in vivo
key_findings.finding: GMs can regulate angiogenesis through metabolites like LPS, lipoteichoic acid, and butyrate, which affect VEGF expression and endothelial cell function. Some bacteria promote angiogenesis, while others inhibit it.
Antibiotic use is consistently associated with worse survival and reduced efficacy in patients receiving ICIs, suggesting GMs play a critical role in treatment response.
FMT from responders to ICIs can restore efficacy in non-responders in some cases. Engineered bacteria (e.g., SYNB1891) show promise in activating innate immunity in combination with ICIs.

study_summary_A.problem_or_question: The paper addresses the problem that many patients do not respond to or develop resistance to ICIs and antiangiogenic therapies. It seeks to understand how the gut microbiome influences these treatments and explores potential methods to leverage GMs to improve therapeutic outcomes.
study_summary_A.research_scope: The paper focuses on the interaction between gut microbes (GMs) and cancer therapy, specifically examining their role in modulating immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) and antiangiogenic agents. It covers human physiology, tumor microenvironment (TME), preclinical models, and clinical trials involving various solid tumors.
study_summary_A.work_summary: This perspective article reviews the complex relationship between the gut microbiome and cancer treatment efficacy. It discusses how GMs influence both angiogenesis in the tumor microenvironment and the response to immune checkpoint blockade. The authors summarize current strategies for manipulating GMs—including probiotics, fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), dietary interventions, and engineered bacteria—to enhance the effectiveness of combined ICI and antiangiogenic therapies. The paper also highlights the challenges and opportunities for translating these findings into clinical practice, noting safety concerns and the need for more specific mechanistic understanding.

chapter_plan.reader_objective: 使读者清晰理解微生物群调制 ICI 疗效的三大核心生物学路径，掌握关键菌种/代谢物的作用靶点与浓度阈值，并能准确评估临床前因果证据与人类观察性数据的证据等级差异，从而在撰写综述时合理界定机制假设与确证事实的边界。
chapter_plan.thesis: 肠道微生物群通过免疫启动（DC/T 细胞互作）、代谢物信号（SCFAs、肌苷、色氨酸/胆汁酸受体通路）及屏障完整性/细菌易位三大路径调制实体瘤 ICI 疗效；临床前模型确立了明确的因果链条，但人类数据多为观察性关联，需严格区分物种差异与肿瘤类型特异性，避免将动物模型结论直接外推为临床事实。肌苷等关键代谢物的人类肿瘤微环境浓度数据尚缺，现有证据主要依赖血浆相关性与小鼠模型。

paragraph_briefs.development: 比较双歧杆菌、阿克曼氏菌与肠球菌对 DC 表型（MHC-I/II、CD80/86、IL-12 分泌）的调控差异；引入 SagA 肽聚糖水解酶/NOD2 轴作为分子开关，说明特定菌株如何突破稳态触发 DC 活化。
paragraph_briefs.point: DC 成熟是免疫启动的限速步骤，不同共生菌通过 PRRs/NOD2 轴差异化调控 DC 表型。

paragraph_briefs.development: 阐述微生物抗原与肿瘤新抗原序列同源性如何诱导预存记忆 T 细胞克隆；结合肌苷通过 UBA6 抑制解除 MHC-I 类分子加工限制的非经典途径，说明微生物如何通过双重靶向增强内在免疫原性。
paragraph_briefs.point: 分子模拟假说提供交叉反应性 T 细胞扩增的机制桥梁，补充传统 DC-T 细胞轴之外的非经典路径。

paragraph_briefs.development: 对比无菌鼠/人源化鼠定植实验的强因果效力与人类队列的观察性局限；强调物种间 DC 发育轨迹与 TLR 信号通路的差异，警示跨物种外推的局限性。
paragraph_briefs.point: 临床前因果证据与人类观察性数据的证据等级差异警示直接外推风险。

units.synthesis: 免疫启动路径揭示了共生菌如何通过 PRR/NOD2 轴与分子模拟桥接先天与适应性免疫，构成 ICI 疗效增强的第一道防线。然而，该路径的效能高度依赖宿主 DC 发育轨迹与 TLR 信号基线，临床前强因果链在人类中多表现为观察性关联。
units.transition: 除细胞互作外，可溶性小分子同样构成关键的远程调制网络，其效能取决于受体亲和力与微环境浓度阈值。
units.unit_title: 免疫启动路径：树突状细胞成熟与 T 细胞交叉反应/致敏

paragraph_briefs.development: 详述丁酸/丙酸在生理黏膜浓度下促进 Treg 分化，而在肿瘤炎症微环境中通过 HDAC 抑制上调 MHC-I 并增强 CD8+ T 细胞杀伤力；引用定量浓度数据说明阈值效应与微环境 pH/氧分压的情境依赖性。强调人类 TME 内 SCFA 直接浓度数据缺失，现有证据基于粪便/血浆样本。
paragraph_briefs.point: SCFAs 的浓度依赖性与情境依赖性呈现双刃剑效应。

paragraph_briefs.development: 阐述肌苷作为嘌呤代谢中间产物，既可通过腺苷 A2A 受体（A2AR）促进 Th1 分化，又直接进入肿瘤细胞抑制泛素激活酶 UBA6，解除对 MHC-I 类分子加工的限制，从而增强内在免疫原性。明确指出人类肿瘤微环境内肌苷绝对浓度数据尚未测定，现有证据依赖 CheckMate 025 血浆相关性（中位 OS 33 个月 vs. 22 个月）与小鼠模型验证。
paragraph_briefs.point: 肌苷通过 A2AR 与 UBA6 的双向靶向克服 ICI 耐药，但人类 TME 浓度数据缺失。

paragraph_briefs.development: 对比促炎/抗炎分支：犬尿氨酸激活 AhR 促进 Treg/MDSC 积累导致耐药；而吲哚衍生物（IPA/IAA）激活 AhR 或核受体（FXR/TGR5）可逆转免疫抑制；胆汁酸（UDCA vs DCA/LCA）呈现剂量与受体依赖的双刃剑效应。
paragraph_briefs.point: 色氨酸-AhR 轴与胆汁酸核受体的双向免疫调节。

units.synthesis: 代谢物信号揭示了远程调制的生化基础，其效能高度依赖受体表达谱、浓度阈值与微环境理化参数。这些可溶性信号构成了连接肠道生态与远端 TME 的分子桥梁，但其双向效应要求精准干预而非盲目补充。人类肿瘤微环境内代谢物绝对浓度数据缺失，现有证据主要依赖外周样本相关性与临床前模型。
units.transition: 代谢物信号的"泄漏"程度与局部微环境重塑，根本上受制于肠道物理屏障的完整性；屏障破坏引发的细菌易位成为第三条关键调制路径。
units.unit_title: 代谢物信号通路：受体介导的表观遗传与转录重编程

paragraph_briefs.development: 分析紧密连接蛋白（ZO-1, Occludin）与杯状细胞黏液层在维持生态位中的作用；对比健康稳态与菌群失调（如抗生素暴露、高脂饮食）下的通透性变化及其对循环内毒素水平的直接影响。
paragraph_briefs.point: 屏障完整性决定微生物信号的系统性"泄漏"阈值。

paragraph_briefs.development: 阐述易位细菌如何被引流淋巴结捕获并触发远端抗肿瘤免疫景观重塑；结合空间多组学与活体成像证据说明易位的时空动态，并指出同一易位事件可能同时驱动抗肿瘤效应与 irAEs 发生。
paragraph_briefs.point: 易位细菌被次级淋巴器官捕获后触发远端抗肿瘤免疫或引发 irAEs。

paragraph_briefs.development: 探讨屏障修复剂、靶向益生菌清除易位病原体及空间控释递送系统的转化前景；强调需在恢复屏障稳态与保留有益信号"泄漏"之间取得平衡。
paragraph_briefs.point: 屏障修复策略与易位调控的临床转化潜力。

units.synthesis: 屏障完整性是决定微生物信号系统性"泄漏"的物理闸门；易位事件既可重塑远端抗肿瘤免疫景观，也可能诱发 irAEs，凸显了物理屏障在调制治疗窗口中的核心地位。
units.transition: 三大路径共同构成微生物调制 ICI 疗效的网络，但临床前因果链与人类观察性数据之间存在显著证据鸿沟，需明确界定转化边界。
units.unit_title: 屏障功能与细菌易位：物理屏障破坏与局部/系统性免疫重塑

paragraph_briefs.development: 对比无菌鼠/人源化鼠定植实验的强因果效力与人类队列（如 P0613, P0490）的观察性局限；强调物种间 DC 发育轨迹、TLR 信号基线与肿瘤微环境理化参数的差异，警示直接外推风险。
paragraph_briefs.point: 临床前因果链的强效力与人类观察性数据的异质性形成证据鸿沟。

paragraph_briefs.development: 分析黑色素瘤、NSCLC、RCC、CRC 等癌种间菌群基线、ICI 响应阈值与代谢物阈值的显著差异；指出 16S rRNA 与宏基因组测序、样本采集与存储流程的不一致如何放大结果异质性。
paragraph_briefs.point: 肿瘤类型特异性与测序方法学差异加剧结果不可比性。

paragraph_briefs.development: 总结当前证据等级（临床前强因果 vs 人类中等/低确定性观察），提出 III 期 RCT、多中心标准化采样、配对血清/肿瘤组织代谢物定量及 AI 辅助多组学整合的优先事项；明确当前仅支持谨慎的抗生素管理与探索性 FMT，不支持常规益生菌推荐。
paragraph_briefs.point: 转化准备度评估：从概念验证到标准化 RCT 的必经之路。

units.synthesis: 三大调制路径共同构成微生物影响 ICI 疗效的网络，但临床前强因果链与人类观察性数据之间存在显著证据鸿沟。严格区分物种差异、肿瘤类型特异性与方法学异质性，是合理界定机制假设与确证事实边界的必要前提。人类 TME 代谢物定量数据缺失限制机制外推，个体异质性（饮食、药物）干扰机制解析。
units.transition: 本章机制解析为后续章节评估干预策略可行性、安全性与临床转化路线图奠定了生物学与证据等级基础。

open_questions: What is the specific molecular mechanism by which inosine enhances tumour immunogenicity?

The supplied material does not provide data on inosine concentrations, which is a specific requirement of the gap question. Furthermore, while the success criteria allow for serum data, the gap question prioritizes concentrations 'inside the human tumour microenvironment'; this study measured peripheral plasma and fecal concentrations, not intratumoral tissue concentrations. Therefore, the physiological levels of SCFAs and inosine specifically within the tumour tissue remain unaddressed. The success criterion for quantitative data of specific metabolites is partially met for SCFAs in plasma but unmet for inosine and tumour tissue.
需要寻找具体的研究，这些研究必须满足两个条件：1) 从人类 ICI 队列中鉴定出特定的关联菌株；2) 通过实验手段（如无菌小鼠定植该特定分离株、体外共培养或特定代谢物补充）直接验证该菌株对 ICI 疗效的因果功能。目前的材料仅提供了物种水平的临床关联、菌株水平的基因组预测或治疗性益生菌的临床试验，未提供“从人源队列分离并实验验证功能”的直接案例。

While the study links the specific strain to immune changes in patients, the human data primarily demonstrates pharmacodynamic associations (pre-post treatment changes or responder vs. non-responder comparisons) rather than causal validation of the specific immune mechanism (e.g., proving TLR4-mediated DC maturation) within the human patients themselves. The deep mechanistic pathway (TLR4, M2-M1 repolarization) is validated in preclinical models, leaving the human mechanistic validation at the level of immune marker modulation consistent with the hypothesis but not experimentally proven beyond correlation in the clinical cohort.

fulfillment_judgment.outline_action: Search for the primary publication or supplementary data of the CheckMate 025 metabolomics analysis (referenced as Hakimi et al. or similar in the field) to extract specific inosine concentration values (μM) associated with response. Look for studies specifically quantifying SCFAs (e.g., butyrate, acetate) in human tumor tissue or serum correlated with ICB response, as this study focuses on purine metabolism. Investigate whether any studies have directly measured intratumoral inosine concentrations in human biopsies pre- and post-ICI to address the TME component of the gap.
fulfillment_judgment.remaining_gap: The supplied text does not provide the specific quantitative concentration values (e.g., μM, ng/mL) for inosine in human plasma or tumor tissue, only stratifying patients by median levels. The gap question asks for concentrations inside the human tumour microenvironment, but this study measured plasma/serum, not direct intratumoral concentrations in humans. Additionally, there is no quantitative data provided for SCFAs in human tumor or serum linked to ICI outcomes, despite their mention as relevant microbiome metabolites in the introduction. The specific physiological ranges defining 'high' vs 'low' inosine remain unspecified in this text.
useful_material: This study reports a re-analysis of plasma metabolomic data from renal cell carcinoma (RCC) patients in the CheckMate 025 trial (nivolumab vs everolimus), finding that higher baseline plasma inosine levels correlate with longer overall survival specifically in the nivolumab arm (median OS 33 months vs 22 months for high vs low groups). The authors confirm that metabolic profiling of ICB-treated human cancers supports the association between inosine levels and ICB sensitivity. Mechanistically, the study identifies that inosine directly inhibits the ubiquitin-activating enzyme UBA6 in tumor cells, enhancing tumor immunogenicity and MHC-I expression, rather than acting primarily on T cells. This provides a specific molecular link between a microbiota-associated metabolite (inosine) and tumor-intrinsic resistance to ICB.

fulfillment_judgment.outline_action: Retrieve the primary study cited as reference (182) in this review to extract specific quantitative plasma SCFA concentration data linked to ICI outcomes. Conduct a targeted search for primary literature measuring inosine and SCFA concentrations specifically within human tumour tissue (TME) rather than just circulation. Evaluate whether available quantitative data meets the threshold for predictive versus prognostic classification as outlined in this review's framework.
fulfillment_judgment.remaining_gap: The supplied text does not provide the specific quantitative concentration values (e.g., μM, ng/mL) for inosine or SCFAs in human serum, plasma, or tumour tissue required by the success criteria. It states 'higher concentrations' were associated with outcomes but does not report the measured numbers. Furthermore, the text discusses plasma and fecal concentrations but does not report measured physiological concentrations inside the human tumour microenvironment (TME).
useful_material: Section 6.3 identifies microbiome-derived metabolites, specifically short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) and inosine, as candidate blood-accessible biomarkers linked to immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) efficacy. The authors report that higher concentrations of fecal and plasma SCFAs were associated with longer progression-free survival in patients treated with nivolumab or pembrolizumab, citing reference (182). The text also notes preclinical evidence that microbiome-derived inosine can enhance response to checkpoint blockade (184). The review provides a conceptual framework for distinguishing predictive from prognostic biomarkers, which is relevant for interpreting metabolite-ICI correlations.

This study explicitly states that paired measurements of candidate metabolites, including short-chain fatty acids and amino-acid pools, across stool, portal or peripheral blood, tumor tissue, and tumor interstitial fluid are lacking in the current literature. Regarding inosine, the authors describe it as a proof-of-principle where a microbiota-derived metabolite enhanced checkpoint-blockade efficacy and T-cell function in mice, citing preclinical evidence rather than human tumor concentrations. For SCFAs, the study reports quantitative data only from fecal samples in non-nutritive sweetener intervention trials (e.g., no change in fecal SCFAs after sucralose/aspartame in Ahmad et al. 2020; lower fecal butyrate associated with NNS intake in Farup et al. 2019), without linking these fecal levels to human tumor microenvironment concentrations or ICI outcomes.

The authors provide a detailed mechanistic explanation of how inosine modulates immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) response, specifically through adenosine A2A receptor-dependent activation of CD8+ T cells and Th1 differentiation, and promotion of M1-like macrophage polarization. The text references a Phase-2 clinical trial where inosine supplementation (0.2 g orally three times/day) was combined with PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors and chemotherapy in a mixed solid-tumor population, noting a mild enhancement of efficacy, though CRC-specific outcomes were not separately reported. Crucially, the authors explicitly state that human data regarding spatial redistribution and quantitative levels of inosine in CRC are currently missing or under-characterized compared to other metabolites like short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), confirming the scarcity of the requested data type.

fulfillment_judgment.outline_action: Search for metabolomics studies that specifically profile intratumoral tissue samples from ICI-treated patients to capture TME-specific concentrations. Conduct a targeted search for 'inosine' combined with 'tumour microenvironment' and 'immune checkpoint inhibitor' to find if inosine has been quantified in human tumour tissue or serum in this context. Consider reviewing metabolomic profiling papers that cover broader panels than SCFAs to check for inosine inclusion.
fulfillment_judgment.remaining_gap: The supplied material does not provide data on inosine concentrations, which is a specific requirement of the gap question. Furthermore, while the success criteria allow for serum data, the gap question prioritizes concentrations 'inside the human tumour microenvironment'; this study measured peripheral plasma and fecal concentrations, not intratumoral tissue concentrations. Therefore, the physiological levels of SCFAs and inosine specifically within the tumour tissue remain unaddressed. The success criterion for quantitative data of specific metabolites is partially met for SCFAs in plasma but unmet for inosine and tumour tissue.
useful_material: This prospective cohort study (n=52) measured quantitative concentrations of short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) in human plasma and fecal samples from patients with solid tumors treated with PD-1 inhibitors. The authors reported median concentrations in μmol/g for multiple SCFAs, linking them to immune checkpoint inhibitor outcomes. Specifically, fecal propionic acid concentrations were significantly higher in responders (median 172.6 μmol/g) compared to nonresponders (median 103.6 μmol/g), and high fecal propionic acid was independently associated with longer progression-free survival (multivariate HR, 0.07; 95% CI, 0.03-0.19). Plasma isovaleric acid was also significantly higher in responders (median 0.3 μmol/g) vs nonresponders (median 0.0 μmol/g) and associated with progression-free survival (HR, 0.38; 95% CI, 0.14-0.99). Other measured SCFAs included acetic, butyric, valeric, isobutyric, hydroangelic, caproic, and succinic acids in both matrices. This provides quantitative metabolite data in a systemic biofluid (plasma) correlated with ICI efficacy, addressing the 'serum' and 'quantitative data' aspects of the success criteria for SCFAs.

This study identifies inosine and short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) as microbiota-derived metabolites with biological relevance to T-cell differentiation and immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) efficacy, citing proof-of-principle evidence for inosine in mice (Section 5.1).

The authors explicitly state that paired measurements of candidate metabolites, including SCFAs and amino-acid pools, in stool, portal or peripheral blood, tumor tissue, and tumor interstitial fluid are currently lacking in the literature (Section 5.1).

Table 1 provides quantitative data on fecal SCFAs from human intervention studies (e.g., Ahmad et al. 2020; Kwok et al. 2024), though these were conducted in healthy adults without ICI therapy and measured stool rather than tumor concentrations.

Section 3 details challenges in exposure assessment and metabolite measurement, noting that urinary biomarkers exist for some compounds but direct tumor microenvironment quantification remains a methodological gap.

The review distinguishes between contextual microbiome-ICI evidence (where inosine/SCFAs are mentioned as affecting T-cell fitness) and direct NNS-ICI evidence, clarifying that metabolite-ICI links often derive from studies not testing the specific exposure of interest (Section 6.1).

This narrative review establishes a mechanistic framework (Microbiome → Metabolites → Immune Modulation → TME State → ICI Response) linking gut microbial metabolites to immune checkpoint inhibitor efficacy. The authors detail short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) mechanisms, including G-protein-coupled receptor binding and histone deacetylase inhibition, and explain that SCFA immune outcomes are concentration-dependent and microenvironment-specific (e.g., physiological mucosal concentrations favor Treg induction, while tumor-inflamed environments may favor CD8+ T-cell enhancement). Crucially, the authors explicitly state that the concentration-response relationship for SCFAs in human tumor-bearing contexts has not been characterized. The text does not contain any mention of inosine.

examples.attribution: Li et al. (2019) / CheckMate 025 队列分析
examples.conditions: 人群：接受Nivolumab或Everolimus治疗的晚期肾细胞癌患者；分组依据：基线血浆肌苷水平的中位数分为高/低两组；指标：总生存期（OS）。
examples.finding: 在肾细胞癌（RCC）患者队列（CheckMate 025试验，Nivolumab治疗组 n=394, Everolimus对照组 n=349）中，通过非靶向代谢组学分析发现，只有肌苷水平与免疫检查点阻断（ICB）的总生存期（OS）显著相关。具体而言，基线血浆肌苷水平较高的Nivolumab治疗患者中位OS为33个月，而低肌苷水平患者的中位OS为22个月。这种关联仅在Nivolumab（抗PD-1）治疗组中存在，而在Everolimus（mTOR抑制剂）治疗组中未观察到显著差异。
examples.use_in_review: 提供人类实体瘤患者血浆中肌苷浓度与ICI疗效的相关性数据，特别是生存期差异。

examples.attribution: 本研究 (Inhibition of UBA6 by inosine...)
examples.conditions: 动物模型：B16-F0黑色素瘤小鼠，ICI治疗前后对比；临床队列：22名接受Sintilimab（抗PD-1）治疗的实体瘤患者，基于肿瘤组织UBA6蛋白表达（IHC评分）分组；指标：肿瘤体积、生存率、总体响应率（ORR）、UBA6蛋白表达水平。

examples.conditions: 研究人群：NSCLC队列（n=20，一线治疗，PD-L1 TPS ≥ 50%，无既往抗PD-1暴露）；黑色素瘤队列（n=20，一线治疗，允许既往辅助抗PD-1但需停药>6个月）。干预措施：单次健康供体粪便微生物移植（FMT，口服胶囊）后紧接着启动ICI治疗。NSCLC组使用帕博利珠单抗（pembrolizumab）单药；黑色素瘤组使用纳武利尤单抗（nivolumab）联合伊匹木单抗（ipilimumab）。
examples.finding: 在NSCLC队列中，FMT联合抗PD-1治疗的客观缓解率（ORR）为80%（16/20），超过了预设的64%主要终点阈值。在黑色素瘤队列中，FMT联合抗PD-1加抗CTLA-4（双ICI）治疗的ORR为75%（15/20）。关于毒性信号，在黑色素瘤双ICI组中观察到严重不良事件（AEs）的发生率较高且起病更早：13名患者（65%）经历了3级或更高级别的AEs，其中腹泻或结肠炎是最常见的3级及以上AE（20%的患者），另有15%的患者出现心肌炎。严重毒性的中位起病时间为开始抗PD-1和抗CTLA-4治疗后40天，早于文献报道的60天。相比之下，NSCLC单药抗PD-1组无3级或以上AEs发生。
examples.use_in_review: 提供FMT联合免疫检查点抑制剂（ICI）在非小细胞肺癌（NSCLC）和黑色素瘤中的具体客观缓解率（ORR），以及双免疫检查点抑制剂（dual ICI）治疗下的毒性信号特征。

question_material.explanation: 该研究通过FMT-LUMINate II期临床试验评估了FMT联合ICI在两种不同癌症背景下的临床活性与安全性。结果显示，FMT显著提高了NSCLC患者对单药抗PD-1治疗的反应率（80%），并改善了黑色素瘤患者对双免疫检查点阻断（抗PD-1+抗CTLA-4）的反应率（75%）。然而，在黑色素瘤双ICI背景下，FMT联合治疗伴随着更高的免疫相关不良事件（irAEs）风险，特别是心肌炎和早期发作的严重毒性。这种毒性信号与特定供体来源的微生物群（富含Prevotella spp.）有关，且仅在双ICI背景下出现，而在单药抗PD-1背景下未观察到类似毒性。这表明FMT的安全性与特定的ICI治疗方案及供体微生物特征存在交互作用。

fulfillment_judgment.outline_action: 1. Cite this meta-analysis as evidence of the current lack of completed Phase III data in peer-reviewed literature up to late 2024. 2. Perform a direct, current search of ClinicalTrials.gov and WHO ICTRP using terms 'microbiome', 'FMT', 'probiotic', 'Phase III', 'immune checkpoint inhibitor', and 'solid tumor' to identify any ongoing or recently completed trials not yet published. 3. Cross-reference any identified registry records with the studies included in this meta-analysis to ensure no duplication or missed data. 4. If no Phase III trials are found in registries, use this paper's conclusion ('larger-scale RCTs... are required') to substantiate the claim of absence.
fulfillment_judgment.remaining_gap: While this meta-analysis confirms the absence of completed large-scale Phase III RCTs in the published literature and searched registries up to September 2024, it does not rule out ongoing Phase III trials that have not yet reported results or were not captured in the search. The success criterion requires confirming absence through registry searches; this paper reports doing so, but a direct, current verification of ClinicalTrials.gov for 'Phase III' status trials (ongoing or completed without publication) remains necessary to fully close the gap.

useful_material.content: The meta-analysis searched ClinicalTrials.gov, chictr.org, and major oncology conference abstracts up to September 30, 2024, identifying 10 studies (164 patients). Among these, 5 were Phase I, 4 were Phase II–III, and 1 unspecified. Only 3 were RCTs (Spreafico et al. Phase 2/3, Glitza et al. Phase 1, Dizman et al. Phase 1). No completed large-scale Phase III RCTs reporting primary efficacy outcomes (OS/PFS/ORR) were identified in the included literature.
useful_material.relevance: Directly addresses the gap question by reporting the absence of completed large-scale Phase III RCTs in the searched literature and registries up to the search date.

useful_material.content: The authors conclude that 'larger-scale randomized controlled trials with long-term follow-up are required to confirm and optimize treatment protocols' and note 'the absence of randomized controlled trials was notable' (referring to large/definitive trials).
useful_material.relevance: Supports the confirmation of absence criterion by explicitly stating the field's need for such trials, implying they do not currently exist in a completed, reportable state.

useful_material.content: Pooled ORR was 43% across included studies (mostly Phase I/II). In the three included RCTs, heterogeneity increased, and the pooled Risk Ratio for ORR was 1.31 (95% CI: 0.58–2.98), crossing 1 (not statistically significant).
useful_material.relevance: Provides context on why Phase III data is needed; current RCT evidence is insufficient to establish efficacy, reinforcing the gap's importance.

useful_material: This review article systematically catalogs clinical trials of FMT combined with ICIs in solid tumors (Table 1), listing 29 trials with their phases, tumor types, and primary outcomes. All listed trials are Phase I, Phase Ib, Phase I/II, or Phase II; none are Phase III. The review explicitly states in Section 5.1 that 'large-scale, multi-center randomized controlled trials (RCTs) are essential to comprehensively evaluate the therapeutic potential of FMT in augmenting ICI therapy,' identifying this as a future research direction rather than completed evidence. The review discusses one randomized controlled trial (NCT03817125, SER-401) that was modified from a four-arm to a two-arm placebo-controlled design, but this was not Phase III and showed lower response rates in the intervention group versus placebo. The review provides mechanistic explanations for heterogeneous trial results (microbiota composition, metabolites, TME remodeling, signaling pathways) and outlines what future Phase III trials should measure (OS, PFS, ORR, quality of life).

This study explicitly characterizes the current evidence level for fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) combined with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) as predominantly derived from early-phase, single-arm studies. It identifies a 2026 phase 2 randomized controlled trial (TACITO trial in metastatic renal cell carcinoma) as a pivotal step but notes it did not formally meet its primary endpoint. The authors conclude that large-scale phase 3 randomized controlled trials are critically needed and urgently prioritized to validate efficacy across tumor types, implying their absence in the published literature up to March 2026. The text also summarizes efficacy outcomes from available phase 1/2 trials (e.g., ORR of 80% in NSCLC, 75% in melanoma, 43% pooled in solid tumors) to contextualize the need for higher-level evidence.

fulfillment_judgment.outline_action: Resolve the acquisition or judgment issue before making a scientific absence claim.
fulfillment_judgment.remaining_gap: What are the measured physiological concentrations of inosine and SCFAs inside the human tumour microenvironment correlating with ICI response?

fulfillment_judgment.outline_action: Search for primary metabolomics studies in ICI-treated cohorts that specifically report intratumoral or paired serum-stool-tumor concentrations of inosine and SCFAs, rather than reviews. Prioritize literature citing the inosine proof-of-principle study (reference 47 in this text) for human validation attempts. Investigate studies using spatial metabolomics or mass spectrometry imaging on tumor resections from immunotherapy patients.
fulfillment_judgment.remaining_gap: No prospective human studies reporting absolute concentrations (e.g., μmol/g or μM) of inosine or specific SCFAs in paired tumor tissue and serum/stool from ICI-treated solid tumor patients are identified in this material. The text confirms that such paired measurements are currently lacking in the literature it reviewed.
useful_material: The authors explicitly state that for most candidate microbiota-derived metabolites, including short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) and amino-acid pools, paired measurements in stool, portal or peripheral blood, tumor tissue, and tumor interstitial fluid are lacking.

Inosine is identified as a proof-of-principle microbiota-derived metabolite that enhanced checkpoint-blockade efficacy and T-cell function in mice, though human intratumoral concentration data is not provided.

Contextual microbiome-ICI evidence is cited indicating that fiber-associated microbial functions, inosine, and SCFAs can affect T-cell differentiation and metabolic fitness, establishing biological relevance without providing the requested human concentration data.
The limitations section notes 'limited direct measurement of candidate metabolites within tumors' as a specific evidence gap.

Discussion on biomarker-based exposure assessment using liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC–MS/MS) provides methodological context for how metabolite quantification might be approached, though applied here to sweeteners rather than tumor metabolites.

This study prospectively measured absolute concentrations of specific short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) including propionic, butyric, acetic, and valeric acids in fecal samples from 11 NSCLC patients treated with nivolumab, reporting quantification in µmol/g (e.g., propionic acid median 7.14 µmol/g in long responders vs 2.56 µmol/g in early progressors). The authors correlated these fecal metabolite levels with clinical response (progression-free survival), finding that higher SCFA concentrations were associated with long-term benefit, while volatile organic compounds like 2-pentanone and tridecane were associated with early progression.

fulfillment_judgment.outline_action: Use this study to support the association between fecal SCFA levels (specifically propionate) and ICI clinical outcomes and intratumoral immune gene signatures. Cite the limitation that intratumoral metabolite concentrations were not directly quantified. Continue searching for studies that explicitly perform metabolomics on tumor biopsy samples paired with stool or serum in ICI-treated cohorts to fulfill the intratumoral quantification criterion.
fulfillment_judgment.remaining_gap: The success criteria require absolute concentrations (e.g., μmol/g or μM) of inosine or specific SCFAs in paired tumor tissue and serum/stool from ICI-treated solid tumor patients. This study provides fecal SCFA concentrations and correlates them with outcomes and tumor gene expression, but it does not report the measured physiological concentrations of these metabolites inside the human tumor microenvironment. The specific intratumoral metabolite quantification remains unaddressed in the supplied text.
useful_material: This prospective study enrolled 39 patients with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (mNSCLC) treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI) alone or with chemotherapy. The authors collected fecal and tumor samples prior to ICI initiation. Fecal short-chain fatty acids (SCFA) were measured by LC-MS/MS, and tumoral transcriptome profiling was performed via RNA sequencing. The study reported that high levels of fecal propionate correlated with significantly longer overall survival (p=0.02) and were increased in the high fiber diet group compared to the low fiber group. At the tumor level, RNA sequencing demonstrated upregulation of humoral and adaptive immune responses in the high fiber group. However, the text specifies fecal SCFA measurement and tumor transcriptomics; it does not explicitly report absolute concentrations of SCFAs or inosine within the tumor tissue itself.

fulfillment_judgment.outline_action: Cite this study as primary evidence for human strain-level metagenomic associations with ICI outcomes. Explicitly note the distinction between strain-level genomic association (fulfilled) and experimental functional validation (remaining gap). Search for subsequent studies that may have isolated the identified SGBs or gene clusters for gnotobiotic validation. Consider this material as a benchmark for strain-resolution methodology in future cohort comparisons.
fulfillment_judgment.remaining_gap: While this study establishes strain-level associations and predicts function via gene content, it does not provide experimental validation of the specific strain functions (e.g., isolating the beneficial E. coli strain to confirm causal mechanisms in vivo). The strain-level findings are currently limited to E. coli and F. prausnitzii due to abundance constraints, leaving other species (e.g., Bifidobacterium mentioned in the gap question) unaddressed at this resolution. Additionally, the primary cohort is lung cancer-specific; broader validation across tumor types for these specific strain markers is needed to confirm generalizability.
useful_material: This prospective human cohort study (n=54 metagenome, n=49 metabolome) utilized strain-level metagenomic resolution (StrainPhlAn, PanPhlAn) to distinguish specific strains of Escherichia coli and Faecalibacterium prausnitzii linked to ICI outcomes. It identified specific species-level genome bins (SGBs), such as F. prausnitzii SGB15342 and SGB15316_group, that were significantly enriched in the long-term benefit group compared to resistance. For E. coli, it distinguished harmful gene families (toxin-antitoxin, stress response) present in resistance/irAE groups from beneficial clusters absent in benefit groups. These strain-level genomic variations correlated with clinical phenotypes (efficacy and irAEs) independent of species-level abundance, directly addressing the requirement for strain-resolution linked to ICI outcomes.

This study analyzed four human fecal metagenomic cohorts (Ashray_2024, Lee_2022, Matson_2018, Frankel_2017) comprising patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI). The authors developed a deep learning model (BioP-VAE) using gene-level microbial abundance features (RPKM) and compared them against taxonomic abundance features at family, genus, species, and strain levels. The results showed that gene-level features outperformed all taxonomic levels for predicting ICI response (AUC 0.89 vs. strain-level AUC 0.72 in Ashray_2024). However, among taxonomic features, strain-level abundance provided better predictive performance for 12-month progression-free survival than species-level abundance (AUC 0.85 vs. 0.67). Feature attribution identified specific microbial genes and pathways (e.g., nitrilase in responders, lipoic acid metabolism in non-responders) and taxa (e.g., Ruminococcaceae, Desulfovibrionaceae) associated with outcomes, suggesting functional capacity is more predictive than taxonomy.

This study performed shotgun metagenomic sequencing on stool samples from 165 ICI-naive melanoma patients across five cohorts, integrated with 147 public samples. The authors identified a panel of species associated with responders, including Bifidobacterium pseudocatenulatum, Roseburia spp., and Akkermansia muciniphila, but explicitly stated no single species was a fully consistent biomarker across studies. While the methods section notes the use of bioBakery 3 which includes strain-level profiling tools (StrainPhlAn 3.0), the reported results focus on species-level relative abundances and functional potential (KEGG orthologs). The discussion explicitly highlights that microbial uniqueness is encoded at the strain level and calls for future analytical methods to explore individual-specific microbial diversity at that resolution, acknowledging that current methodology generally lacks the ability to characterize microbiome features at the immunological interface or strain level in this context.

fulfillment_judgment.outline_action: Use this material to establish the current state of evidence: species-level associations in human ICI cohorts and strain-level mechanistic validation in preclinical models. Cite the Pal et al. trial as evidence that specific strains can influence ICI outcomes in humans, but explicitly note the methodological gap regarding strain-level baseline prediction in human cohorts. Use the mechanistic details (immune cell changes, cytokines) to support the biological plausibility of strain-specific effects. Highlight the reliance on 16S sequencing in existing human studies as a limitation that necessitates the proposed strain-level validation gap.
fulfillment_judgment.remaining_gap: The specific success criterion requires human cohort studies using strain-level resolution (metagenomics/culturomics) for ICI prediction. The human studies cited in this material relied on 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing, which typically resolves to genus or species level, not strain level. The strain-specific functional validation described was conducted in mouse models, not human cohorts. The human intervention trial (CBM588) validates strain-specific function therapeutically but does not represent a baseline prediction study using strain-resolved microbiome profiling.
useful_material: This review summarizes human clinical correlations between Bifidobacterium abundance and immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) outcomes, specifically citing a 2018 melanoma study (42 patients) and an NSCLC study where responders showed higher Bifidobacterium levels via 16S sequencing. It details a human intervention trial (Pal et al., metastatic renal cell carcinoma) where a specific probiotic strain (CBM588) combined with nivolumab/ipilimumab significantly improved progression-free survival and response rates compared to ICI alone. Additionally, it reports preclinical strain-level differentiation, noting that among four Bifidobacterium strains tested in mice, only specific strains (B.bif_K57, B.bif_K18) synergized with PD-1 inhibitors, while others (B.bif_B06) did not, linked to differences in immune cell infiltration (CD8+ T cells, NK cells) and cytokine profiles (IFN-γ, IL-2).

This study reviews clinical trials investigating defined bacterial isolates and consortia for ICI modulation, listing specific strain-level interventions such as Bifidobacterium animalis lactis (EDP1503) and Clostridium butyricum (CBM 588) with associated NCT numbers (e.g., NCT03595683, NCT03829111). The authors explicitly state that while species-level associations (e.g., Bifidobacterium longum) exist, the signature of favorable bacterial strains based on sequencing has not been consistent across patient studies, and questions remain regarding which assay (metagenomics, culturomics) is ideal to identify specific bacteria. The text notes that clinical trials are ongoing to determine if single bacterial interventions improve antitumor immunity, but confirms that predicting clinical outcomes from specific strains is yet to be determined.

fulfillment_judgment.outline_action: Cite this study as the primary evidence for the existence of human clinical data supporting strain-level over species-level resolution for ICI prediction. Use the specific strain examples (Faecalibacterium, Bifidobacterium) to illustrate intraspecies functional divergence. Highlight the regimen-specificity finding as a critical condition for interpreting strain biomarkers. Note the lack of experimental functional validation as a limitation when discussing mechanistic certainty.
fulfillment_judgment.remaining_gap: While this study fulfills the criterion of finding a human cohort using strain-level resolution linked to ICI outcomes, it does not experimentally validate the microbial functions themselves (e.g., via culturomics, gnotobiotic models, or metabolite measurement) to confirm causality. The functional claims rely on genomic potential inference. Additionally, the external validation was primarily limited to melanoma cohorts for the meta-analysis, and the 'pan-cancer' claim is based on internal rare cancer subtypes.
useful_material: This study performed deep shotgun metagenomic sequencing on baseline fecal samples from a human phase 2 clinical trial cohort (CA209-538, n=106) and a meta-analysis of six external studies (n=364) to link strain-resolved microbial abundances to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) outcomes. The authors constructed a custom strain reference database (1,397 genomes) and demonstrated that strain-level resolution significantly improved machine learning prediction of response and progression-free survival compared to species-level quantification. Specific strain distinctions were highlighted, such as Faecalibacterium strains (positive association) versus Bifidobacterium dentium (negative) compared to Bifidobacterium longum (positive), and Akkermansia muciniphila versus A. muciniphila B. The study also identified genomic functional potentials, noting that positive Ruminococcaceae strains possessed complete acetyl-CoA butyrate pathways while negative ones did not. Furthermore, it established that strain-response signatures are ICB regimen-specific (valid for combination anti-PD-1/CTLA-4 but not anti-PD-1 monotherapy).

This study conducted a prospective observational cohort study (NCT05102773) of metastatic melanoma patients (n=41 assessable) receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), using metagenomic whole-genome shotgun sequencing (MetaPhlAn4/HUMAnN3) to link baseline gut microbiome composition to treatment response (RECIST v1.1) and immune-related adverse events (irAEs). The authors identified specific taxa associated with outcomes, such as Intestinimonas butyriciproducens and Blautia luti with response, and Bifidobacterium dentium with irAEs. The study explicitly notes that while WGS was used, the design establishes association rather than causality or functional validation, and results are primarily reported at the species or genus level (e.g., Lachnospiraceae family, Blautia spp.), with limited strain-level differentiation (e.g., Lachnospira sp. NSJ 43) without functional characterization of those strains.

fulfillment_judgment.outline_action: Use this study to define the specific molecular and cellular mechanism (Ruminococcaceae strain -> CD103+ DCs -> CD8+ T cells) expected in human patients. Cite it as strong preclinical evidence supporting the biological plausibility of strain-specific immune validation. Continue searching for companion publications or subsequent full-text reports from this AACR 2024 abstract group that may detail concurrent human correlative or prospective mechanistic data not captured in this abstract summary.
fulfillment_judgment.remaining_gap: The supplied text explicitly states that the administration and tumor growth inhibition were validated 'in animal models'. While the bacterial strain was isolated from human patients, the text does not explicitly confirm that the specific immune mechanisms (e.g., DC maturation, NFATc1 translocation, TCR repertoire changes) were measured prospectively within the human patients themselves. The success criterion requires a prospective human study linking the strain to a measured immune mechanism in ICI-treated solid tumor patients, which remains unconfirmed based on this abstract alone.
useful_material: This study isolated a novel Ruminococcaceae strain from the feces of patients who responded to PD-1 blockade and demonstrated in animal models that administering this strain with PD-1 blockade inhibited tumor growth. The authors detailed a specific immune mechanism where the bacterial strain promoted IRF8-driven differentiation of CD103+ dendritic cells (DCs) by stimulating multiple Toll-like receptors. These DCs migrated to the tumor microenvironment and tumor-draining lymph nodes, prolonging engagement with cognate antigen-specific CD8+ T cells. This interaction induced CD8+ T cell activation via NFATc1 nuclear translocation, resulting in abundant PD-1+CD8+ T cells with a broader T-cell receptor repertoire. The study establishes a specific 'bacteria-DC-T cell' axis linking a human-derived strain to immune activation mechanisms relevant to checkpoint inhibition.

This study conducted a prospective cohort analysis of lung cancer patients treated with anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy, performing strain-level genomic analysis on specific species (Escherichia coli and Faecalibacterium prausnitzii) using Species-level Genome Bins (SGBs). It identified specific strain variations (e.g., F. prausnitzii SGB15342) associated with clinical efficacy and immune-related adverse events (irAEs). The authors validated microbial metabolite production (short-chain fatty acids like butyrate and propionate) via GC-MS and linked these levels to progression-free survival. Additionally, the study employed bioinformatic mapping to propose a molecular mimicry mechanism, aligning microbial protein sequences with autoimmune and tumor antigen epitopes to explain irAEs and efficacy, respectively.

This study (MET4-IO trial, published 2024) is a prospective human study in ICI-treated solid tumor patients that links specific bacterial species (e.g., Collinsella aerofaciens, Acidaminococcus intestini) from a defined consortium to measured immune mechanisms. It reports treatment-specific circulating IgG responses against the bacteria and uses mass cytometry to identify shifts in circulating immune subsets (increased B cells, FoxP3+ CD4+ T cells; decreased monocytes) associated with high IgG responders. The study design involves administering a specific bacterial consortium (MET4) and measuring engraftment via metagenomics alongside immune readouts, providing an interventional link rather than purely observational correlation.

fulfillment_judgment.outline_action: Cite this study as the primary recent human evidence linking a specific strain (L. mesenteroides CJRB-101) to immune modulation (T-cell activation, myeloid gene upregulation) in ICI-treated solid tumor patients. Use the preclinical data to explain the proposed mechanism (TLR4/M1 repolarization) while explicitly noting that human validation is based on pharmacodynamic markers and spatial profiling rather than direct pathway confirmation. Highlight the distinction between ICI-naïve and ICI-refractory responses to discuss patient selection criteria for future mechanistic studies. Recommend searching for controlled trials or studies with direct mechanistic biopsies (e.g., TLR4 staining) to further close the 'beyond correlation' gap.
fulfillment_judgment.remaining_gap: The human evidence remains primarily pharmacodynamic and associational (pre-post treatment changes in a single-arm trial) rather than definitive causal validation of the specific mechanism (e.g., TLR4 pathway activation by the strain) within patient tissues. The success criterion requires linking strain to mechanism in ICI-treated patients; while this study links strain administration to immune changes, it does not fully prove the strain-specific mechanism in humans 'beyond correlation' without a control arm or direct mechanistic readouts (e.g., TLR4 activation status) in patient samples. Additionally, the mechanistic validation is strongest in the preclinical setting, leaving some uncertainty about the translation of the exact pathway to humans.
useful_material: This study is a prospective, first-in-human Phase I trial (NCT05877430) conducted between 2023 and 2025, evaluating a specific bacterial strain (CJRB-101, Leuconostoc mesenteroides) combined with pembrolizumab in solid tumor patients (NSCLC, HNSCC, melanoma). It directly addresses the gap by linking the administration and stool enrichment of this specific strain to measured immune mechanisms in ICI-treated patients. In human patients, the study reports pharmacodynamic effects including on-treatment upregulation of immune activation genes (CCL5, TLR9, CD3E) in blood/tumor, reduced PD-1+TIM-3+ T cells in PBMCs, and multiplex IHC evidence of enhanced GZB+CD8+ T-cell infiltration in tumor tissue from a responding patient. Stool metagenomics confirmed strain-specific engraftment. While the causal mechanism (TLR4-dependent M2-to-M1 repolarization) was validated in preclinical models (PDX, syngeneic mice, in vitro BMDM), the human data provides prospective interventional evidence linking the strain to immune modulation, though it lacks a placebo-controlled arm to fully isolate the strain's mechanistic contribution from the ICI backbone in humans.

This study is a narrative review focusing on the gut microbiome's influence on hematological malignancies (leukemias, lymphomas, multiple myeloma) and related treatments (HSCT, chemotherapy, CAR-T, ICIs). The authors summarize mechanistic hypotheses linking specific bacteria to immune modulation, such as Akkermansia muciniphila enhancing ICI efficacy via an IL-12-dependent pathway and Bifidobacterium bifidum promoting dendritic cell activation and IFN-γ production. The text explicitly distinguishes between mechanisms observed in solid tumors (e.g., cisplatin toxicity via 3-methylxanthine in epithelial tumors) and hematological cancers, noting that findings do not always translate across cancer types. It also details how antibiotic exposure alters microbiome diversity and treatment response, providing context on confounding factors relevant to immune mechanism studies.

This study identifies specific bacterial strains (Blautia obeum, Blautia massiliensis) within the Lachnospiraceae family that improved ICI effectiveness in a mouse model, contrasting with Agathobacter rectalis which did not. It proposes four specific genomic pathways associated with the effective strains: acetate production (Wood-Ljungdahl pathway), vitamin synthesis (folate B9, cobalamin B12), L-rhamnose synthesis (MAMP priming), and bile acid conversion (Th17/Treg regulation). The human component involves the BEWELL trial, where a black raspberry nectar dietary intervention enriched Lachnospiraceae in the colonic microbiome of patients, providing a human-derived source for the mechanistic investigation.

fulfillment_judgment.outline_action: Cite this study as the primary recent human evidence linking a specific strain (CJRB-101) to immune pharmacodynamics in ICI-treated solid tumors. Use the preclinical data to describe the proposed mechanism (TLR4/M1 polarization) while explicitly qualifying that the human data supports this via correlative immune marker changes (gene expression, flow cytometry) rather than direct mechanistic proof in patients. Highlight the distinction between strain engraftment confirmation and the associative nature of the immune readouts in the Phase I design.
fulfillment_judgment.remaining_gap: While the study links the specific strain to immune changes in patients, the human data primarily demonstrates pharmacodynamic associations (pre-post treatment changes or responder vs. non-responder comparisons) rather than causal validation of the specific immune mechanism (e.g., proving TLR4-mediated DC maturation) within the human patients themselves. The deep mechanistic pathway (TLR4, M2-M1 repolarization) is validated in preclinical models, leaving the human mechanistic validation at the level of immune marker modulation consistent with the hypothesis but not experimentally proven beyond correlation in the clinical cohort.
useful_material: This study is a prospective, first-in-human Phase I trial (NCT05877430, 2023-2025) evaluating a specific bacterial strain, CJRB-101 (Leuconostoc mesenteroides), combined with pembrolizumab in solid tumor patients (NSCLC, HNSCC, melanoma). It meets the temporal and population criteria. The authors confirmed strain-specific engraftment via stool metagenomics (increased L. mesenteroides abundance) and measured immune mechanisms in patients, including upregulation of immune activation genes (CCL5, TLR9, CD3E) in on-treatment samples, reduction of PD-1+TIM-3+ T cells and PMN-MDSCs in peripheral blood, and spatial profiling showing increased GZB+CD8+ T cells in tumor tissue. These data link the specific strain administration to measured immune pharmacodynamic effects in ICI-treated patients.
Identifies specific microbial components linked to ICI efficacy: Akkermansia muciniphila-derived outer membrane protein Amuc_1100 and Bifidobacterium longum.
Describes a specific immune mechanism: Amuc_1100 enhances dendritic cell (DC) maturation and IL-12 secretion via TLR2 signaling, promoting CD8+ T cell-mediated antitumor responses.
Notes exploratory clinical studies using fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) in ICI-refractory patients showing preliminary therapeutic benefit.
Highlights the current limitation that clinical robustness and reproducibility of these microbial biomarkers require validation in larger cohorts.

States that many associations between microbial functional components and host phenotypes remain largely correlative and require validation through prospective cohort studies or human intervention trials.

fulfillment_judgment.outline_action: ['Cite this study as the primary example of moving from human metagenomic association to experimental strain-level functional validation in the context of ICI.', 'Use the SagA/Nod2 mechanism to illustrate how specific bacterial molecules (rather than whole taxa) can be identified and validated as therapeutic adjuvants.', 'Contrast the engineered strain results (E. faecalis-sagA) with wild-type strains to highlight the importance of functional gene presence over taxonomic identity in predicting ICI response.', 'Note the limitation that validation is preclinical (mouse models) and that direct patient-strain-to-mouse transfer was not explicitly described, distinguishing this from culturomics studies that isolate patient-specific strains.']
fulfillment_judgment.remaining_gap: ['While this study validates Enterococcus strains, it does not validate other ICI-associated strains (e.g., Bifidobacterium, Akkermansia) identified in different human cohorts, leaving the broader landscape of strain-level validation incomplete.', 'The strains tested were human-commensal isolates (e.g., Com15) rather than strains directly isolated from specific ICI responder patients in a matched cohort-to-model transfer design.', 'Experimental validation is confined to mouse models; there is no direct experimental validation of these specific strain functions in human clinical trials within this material.']
useful_material: This study experimentally validates the function of ICI-associated bacterial strains (Enterococcus genus) using gnotobiotic and antibiotic-pretreated mouse tumor models (B16-F10 melanoma, MC38, MCA205).

Specific human-commensal strains (e.g., E. faecium Com15) were orally administered to mice and shown to significantly enhance anti-PD-L1, anti-PD-1, and anti-CTLA-4 efficacy compared to non-protective strains (e.g., E. faecalis OG1RF).

The study distinguishes genomic potential from functional validation by identifying the SagA peptidoglycan hydrolase gene, confirming its enzymatic activity in vitro, and proving sufficiency via heterologous expression in E. faecalis and Lactococcus lactis.

Functional validation included metabolite measurement/administration: synthetic Nod2-active muropeptides (MDP-L,D) replicated the antitumor effect, confirming the molecular mechanism beyond live bacterial colonization.
Mechanistic validation established host dependency: the antitumor effect was abrogated in Nod2-/- mice, confirming the specific host receptor pathway required for the strain's function.

This study experimentally validates the functional capacity of responder versus non-responder gut microbiota communities using fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) into gnotobiotic mice, demonstrating that responder microbiota decreases tumor growth following ICI treatment. It identifies specific Amplicon Sequence Variants (ASVs) belonging to genera such as Colidextribacter, Frisingicoccus, Marvinbryantia, and Blautia that overlap between human responders and colonized mice, correlating with tumor size. Crucially for the gap, the authors explicitly state in the Conclusions and Discussion that 'The role of isolate-specific function... has been underappreciated' and that the work 'supports further investigation using isolate-driven models,' indicating that isolation and validation of specific strains from these ASVs had not been performed in this study and remains a necessary future step.

The review explicitly distinguishes between human observational associations and preclinical experimental validation. It documents that while fecal transplantation from human responders to mice recapitulates outcomes (e.g., references [19–21]), these studies often 'did not further identify the specific bacteria whose abundance was associated with immune responses' and highlights the need for 'inoculation with single-lineage bacteria.' It lists specific genera validated in preclinical models via oral gavage (e.g., Bifidobacterium spp., Bacteroides fragilis, Akkermansia muciniphila, Enterococcus hirae) but notes inconsistencies when compared to human cohort data (e.g., Bacteroidales associated with response in some studies, non-response in others). The text explicitly states that 'improvements in the isolation of cultivable bacteria and derivation of individual clones... may represent future steps,' indicating that comprehensive strain-level experimental validation linked to human cohorts is currently lacking or incomplete.

research_question: How does the gut microbiome modulate the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors in solid tumours, and what mechanisms mediate that effect?

shared_outline.purpose: 使读者清晰区分微生物组 -ICI 互作中的观察性关联与干预性因果信号，理解抗生素使用时机（特别是 ICI 启动后 60 天内）与肿瘤类型对疗效影响的异质性，评估 FMT/LBP 在真实世界中的获益/风险比，并明确当前领域缺乏 III 期 RCT 的证据边界及未来优先事项。
shared_outline.scope: 临床证据表明，肠道微生物群扰动（尤其是抗生素与质子泵抑制剂暴露）与实体瘤患者免疫检查点抑制剂（ICI）生存期缩短存在稳健的时序依赖性负相关，其中 ICI 启动后 60 天内的暴露风险最高（HR 1.27），且该效应在头颈部癌、肾细胞癌和乳腺癌中显著，而在肺癌和黑色素瘤中未达统计学显著；粪菌移植（FMT）与活体生物疗法（LBP）在早期临床试验中展现出概念验证潜力（NSCLC ORR 80%, 黑色素瘤 ORR 75%），但伴随显著的毒性信号（双药方案下 65% 发生 3 级+irAE）与供体/患者选择异质性。当前证据层级呈现明显分化：大样本回顾性队列提供了高置信度的预后关联，而干预性数据仍局限于单臂 II 期试验，缺乏随机对照与长期安全性确证。因此，临床转化准备度目前仅支持基于观察性数据的抗生素管理建议，FMT/LBP 等靶向干预仍需等待 III 期随机对照试验验证。
shared_outline.title: 临床证据格局：抗生素时机、FMT 试验与观察性数据

shared_outline.purpose: 使读者掌握预测 ICI 疗效的核心微生物特征清单，理解分类学特征与代谢物在预测效力上的差异，明确当前生物标志物研究的证据层级（观察性关联 vs. 定量验证），并识别限制其临床转化的关键方法学与生物学边界。
shared_outline.scope: 肠道微生物群通过特定的分类学特征（门/属/种/株）与代谢物谱（SCFAs、肌苷等）系统性调节实体瘤 ICI 疗效，但现有证据呈现高度的情境依赖性（癌种、治疗方案、宿主背景）。观察性关联已确立特定菌群与代谢物的预后价值，而定量代谢组学与菌株分辨率研究正推动生物标志物从“物种丰度”向“功能通路”演进；然而，人类肿瘤微环境内代谢物绝对浓度的缺失及跨队列泛化能力的不足，限制了其作为独立临床决策工具的转化就绪度。
shared_outline.title: 微生物特征：预测 ICI 反应的菌分类群与代谢物

shared_outline.purpose: 使读者清晰理解微生物群调制 ICI 疗效的三大核心生物学路径，掌握关键菌种/代谢物的作用靶点与浓度阈值，并能准确评估临床前因果证据与人类观察性数据的证据等级差异，从而在撰写综述时合理界定机制假设与确证事实的边界。
shared_outline.scope: 肠道微生物群通过免疫启动（DC/T 细胞互作）、代谢物信号（SCFAs、肌苷、色氨酸/胆汁酸受体通路）及屏障完整性/细菌易位三大路径调制实体瘤 ICI 疗效；临床前模型确立了明确的因果链条，但人类数据多为观察性关联，需严格区分物种差异与肿瘤类型特异性，避免将动物模型结论直接外推为临床事实。肌苷等关键代谢物的人类肿瘤微环境浓度数据尚缺，现有证据主要依赖血浆相关性与小鼠模型。
shared_outline.title: 机制通路：免疫、代谢与屏障功能的介导作用

shared_outline.purpose: 帮助肿瘤临床医生与研究者区分已验证的临床信号与探索性策略，掌握不同干预手段（FMT、LBP、饮食）的适用人群、安全边界及机制依据，为参与或设计下一代微生物组-ICI 联合试验提供决策参考。
shared_outline.scope: 肠道微生物群干预（FMT、活体生物药/LBP、饮食与代谢物）在增强实体瘤 ICI 疗效方面展现出明确的生物学合理性与初步临床信号，但其临床可靠性受限于供体/菌株异质性、irAE 风险交互作用及缺乏 III 期确证数据。FMT 疗效高度依赖肿瘤类型与 ICI 方案背景（一线单药 vs 耐药挽救），当前证据支持将抗生素管理作为常规实践，而 FMT 与精准菌群工程需严格限定于临床试验或特定难治情境，尚未达到常规临床推荐标准。
shared_outline.title: 治疗干预：FMT、益生菌与饮食调节的可行性

shared_outline.purpose: 帮助读者系统理解当前微生物组-ICI 互作证据的证据等级差异，识别导致结果不一致的方法学与生物学根源，明确区分已验证的临床限制与待探索的机制缺口，并掌握基于证据等级的研究优先事项与转化路线图。
shared_outline.scope: 肠道微生物群对实体瘤 ICI 疗效的调节作用具有坚实的生物学合理性，但现有证据呈现显著的层级分化：观察性关联（如抗生素暴露、特定菌属富集）提供了稳健的效应信号，而干预性证据（如 FMT、活体生物制品）仍局限于早期试验且伴随定植不确定性与安全性考量；跨队列生物标志物难以复现主要源于方法学异质性（测序平台、生信流程、样本采集时序）与生物学情境依赖性（肿瘤类型、宿主基线、给药时序）。系统性检索确认当前无已完成的大规模纯微生物干预 III 期 RCT，TACITO 等试验为 II 期设计且未正式达到主要终点。未来转化需从"单一物种分类学"转向"功能代谢通路"，并依托标准化多中心 RCT 与空间多组学技术，以建立可重复的预测模型与精准干预路径。
